comments.value: The devs have slowly stripping away mod power from actual world creators too, this is absolutely not going to help. Did you know they can’t mod group publics anymore? Or close instances?
I have had issues where people have gatekept me from my own worlds via group instances that is a HORRIBLE idea
This would be the type of thing that would actually murder the game.

I have actively avoided going into group public instances because of the behavior from the moderators in them, constantly breathing down your neck willing to kick you for simply "looking at someone funny" or "having the wrong voice" or some nonsense like that. Not to mention VRChat putting these instances to the top of the world list by default so you're more likely to join those if not paying attention.

This update will make it even easier than it already was to get moderator tools in an instance as you won't need VRChat plus anymore to make a group. Previously they had mentioned they don't want to add AI labels to prevent targeted attacks and such, but with these new moderated publics people can do exactly that for ANYTHING at ANY TIME.

Quest user? Kicked. Mute? Kicked. Under 25? Kicked. OVER 25? Kicked. Transgender? Kicked. Have a boyfriend or girlfriend? Kicked. Doesn't have full body? Kicked.

I'm sure you get the point.

If VRChat wants to keep this feature anyways, at least make it optional, hide the option and make it off by default (and not persistent). Do not let anyone find it easily. It'll be the same as creating a friends+ instance, but public. Only those who needs it will search and find the option.

I have been discussing the related topic of why I think world authors shouldn't have moderation privileges in all instances of their world for 3 years now, in [remove-world-creator-moderation-powers](https://feedback.vrchat.com/feature-requests/p/remove-world-creator-moderation-powers). While I might have become more willy to compromise on what were to happen with "Public" instances, this is a change that I hadn't even considered and I fully welcome it.

If the random person that made the instance is such a bad person that they start power tripping, I fully believe that almost all of us would simply have left the instance by the time their supposed power trip leads them to kicking us. So if anything, this would lead us to get out of bad instances faster and to find a new better one or make our own instances.

Not to mention that you will likely still find plenty of Public instances where the owner simply left hours ago. But maybe it would be useful for that to be highlighted somewhere in the instance list UI?

Most of all, I see this whole feature as a really good thing for world where the owner of the instance might be considered the host. Such as manually run games or minor event instances. This will allow new VRChat users to use those types of worlds and have some control over the instances without needing to get VRC+ and create a group.

@{610d538d5303a82960a415b4|full_name} "If the random person that made the instance is such a bad person that they start power tripping, I fully believe that almost all of us would simply have left the instance by the time their supposed power trip leads them to kicking us"

When the owner just doesn't like you and decides to kick you, you'll have to try to convince your friends to go to another instance, and might not even be able to. It's not that simple as "if the moderation is bad just leave". You'll also lose contact with people you just met but hasn't added yet.

I believe it just doesn't scale well to smaller playerbases

I mean, the entire brazilian community only hangs out in TWO specific worlds, there is just no groups of brazilians in other worlds, never. 

It scales with the group issues i have been dealing and reporting for years. There is a lot of toxic groups in the brazilian community, abusing power and banning people for absolutely no reason, and it just prevents you from playing the game since the entire community only stays in these specific places. You can't join your friends, who don't have anything with this, nor any idea of it.

It'll also be pretty easy for a single user to open multiple public instances of these specific worlds and stay there until it fills and have like 3 instances on his hands. I'm not exaggerating. A few years ago there was a user who monopolized one of these only two worlds we frequent, by buying vrc+ in all his alts and creating different instances of his own. I did reported it, it lasted for months, AND VRCHAT DID NOTHING.

if you got kicked from a group public, then it either was the mod tripping out but it seems unlikely (i can tell because your grammar seems good) or it was something not ok that you said, or an avatar that was not ok, or some troll got the staff to kick you out for no reason.

@{5f4ba617a657d93390b5364b|full_name} most of the reasons are quite unusual to say the liest, such as rival groups, voice, and groups they don't like, what kind of groups you and your friends are joining?

If i may suggest, you should try to enter into the intances of those groups that host events with the "featured" tag on their events, events with such tag are moderated properly

@{60411ec5cc01c21febdcbe37|full_name} I mean, i only join my friends. The world or group hosting the world they are is never relevant. Isn't this the reason most people play? To stay with your friends or to meet new people

The main issue, as i've stated in my other comments, is that the public instance ownership change doesn't scale well for smaller player bases, such as the Brazilian player base.

Why? because, sadly, brazilian streamers only go to TWO specific worlds, which means new players only go to these specific worlds, which means these worlds are the only place we can met new people, which means that's the only place even most trusted users stay, which means it's extremely easy for bad actors to take control, as they already do, since there is nowhere else to go.

Also, a good portion of brazilians do understand english, but we don't usually feel too comfortable interacting with other communities.. Our vrchat world is small~

@{5f4ba617a657d93390b5364b|full_name} to be honest, i play to language exchange and keep practicing english, then I started doing creative things as side projects like avatars worlds.. ecc... 

But i must say, the few times i tried to join italian worlds, as I'm italian, we have few worlds too, maybe 2 or 3, so i was thinking to go to italians with aspirations and attempt "empowering them" with some knowledge on world buildind to see if they go anywhere with it.

I mean, as of late we got "Nina V2" who seems quite good at making worlds in the italian community with Club Italia.

It is quite interesting how you say that those worlds are from streamers as if the streams powered the worlds and vice versa.

I have tried many things in VRChat but i haven't tried streaming VRChat.

Anyhow, going back to the topic, if i were you I'd try to steer your friends to the right instances if this gets acepted or not, i don't usually stay in publics more than 10mins just to see how it is, as i really don't like hearing children so young that they break the TOS.

It is so interesting to hear from someone that doesn't like moderation in group publics, it is the feedback that i would never hear, because I'm always in group publics, and sometimes in friends+.

VRChat has made clear that moderation should be per instance and not per world, I believe is not that big of a deal, you can always join group publics of groups you consider have proper moderators or even create your own instance, if instance owners are trully abusing their power the rest of the users will likely just change to another instance.

My main concern is the lack of accountability combined with how easily these moderation powers would be obtained.

Group Public instances at least have some structure of accountability. Moderators answer to group owners, and group owners have a reputation and community to maintain. Even when the owner is the one moderating, they have some stake in how their group is perceived.

And yet, despite this, moderation in some Group Public instances is already terrible.

So I have very little faith that removing even those limited safeguards will improve things.

Under this proposal, anyone could simply open a Public instance and immediately gain moderation powers. No vetting, no established community, no chain of responsibility, and potentially no reputational consequences for abusing those powers.

If poor moderation is already a problem in a system with at least some accountability, why should we expect better results from a system with even less?

Moderation authority should come with responsibility, not merely the ability to click "Create Instance".

@{639e468235cad333ec7830d8|full_name} Points of view like this make me think you don't actually play the game. Not trying to be rude and i'm sorry if it sounds like that, but it just does not make sense based on my experience.

(I'm talking about this part: "if instance owners are trully abusing their power the rest of the users will likely just change to another instance.")

For example, there is a group here in Brazil where the owner thinks he is the protagonist. He bans everyone for literally ANYTHING. His reputation is the worst, but still, his instance is one of the most populated ones.

People don't care about the instance, people care about being with their friends, that's what VRChat is about for mostly all of us. You just open Social, find somebody you want to join and go. It's not the world or the instance, it's your friend.

A high portion of the active Brazilian players are banned from that specific group i mentioned, and things are so bad to a point where if you say just the group name in public, somebody will join you to share his bad experience there or how he got banned too. Does that matter? No, his instances still always get populated, even besides his deserved terrible reputation.

So, where do i want to get saying this? I mean, things are already bad with the paywall preventing most of bad people from moderating public instances. Giving mod powers to the one who opens a instance is just going to make an existing power abuse issue even worse, since anyone will be able to do it.

@{5f4ba617a657d93390b5364b|full_name} it may be i spend my time in group instances and im a bit disconnected on how the behaviour is in normal publics, they paywall on groups is a real concern that must be adressed asap too, good point

details:
So, I just read the VRChat dev Update from today (https://ask.vrchat.com/t/developer-update-5-november-2026/49298), 

and it says VRChat is going to give Mod permissions to the person who opens a public instance.

I'll be honest here:

IS VRCHAT BLIND? Public instances are the only sanctuaries we could be safe from the Discord Moderador Epidemy that is going on since Groups have been added, and VRChat is getting rid of it by giving mod permissions to the person who opens it??

Even today i got kicked for absolutely no reason because one of these Group Instance moderadors abusing power, and, where did i had to go next? a Public instance, the only place this shit doesn’t happens

This change just confirms VRCHAT IS NOT LOOKING AT THE POWER ABUSE EPIDEMY. I have already made reports on instance moderators abusing power and VRChat never did anything, even when I had video proofs. And now we get this... This is just insane.
title: DO NOT change Mod permissions of public instances
